programme: TFDP1 (the DP partner of E2F, driving G1/S transcription of CCNE1, CDK2, CDK4, PCNA, MYC and the checkpoint gene CDKN1A), KAT5/TIP60 (a CREBBP/TRRAP/EP400/ACTL6A-associated acetyltransferase that acetylates TP53 and H2AZ1 and also targets CDKN1A), and YY1 (a transcription factor whose own target set includes TP53 and MYC, overlapping both other factors) converge on the same p53–p21(CDKN1A)–E2F/Rb checkpoint node — a chromatin-acetylation/cell-cycle-checkpoint module rather than three unrelated regulators.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, this checkpoint/chromatin module is a target of direct viral protein interactions: SARS-CoV-2 Nsp6 is reported to act through an MGA/MAX-adjacent, TFDP1-linked complex to damage cardiomyocytes, ORF3a interacts with YY1, and KAT5 is depleted in SARS-CoV-2-infected neuronal cells alongside markers of oxidative stress and senescence — consistent with the virus disabling or repurposing host cell-cycle/checkpoint control to favor replication and tissue injury.
role_in_b: In ovarian cancer, the same module is co-opted for unchecked proliferation and immune evasion: ZNF146 drives proliferation through TFDP1/DEPDC1B-controlled cell-cycle progression, KAT5 suppresses PD-L1 expression such that its inhibition (e.g., by aspirin) restores anti-tumor immunity, and YY1 is described as a central hub for angiogenesis (via HIF1A), drug resistance, and ferroptosis suppression — i.e. amplification/rewiring of the checkpoint-chromatin axis to sustain growth and evade immune and cell-death control.
shared_axis: A productive viral infection and a malignant epithelial cell face the same obstacle — the p53/p21–E2F/Rb checkpoint that would otherwise arrest the cell cycle — and both recurrently engage TFDP1, KAT5 and YY1 to get past it, the virus by direct protein interaction and the tumor by transcriptional dysregulation of the same three factors.
reasoning: Each of TFDP1, KAT5 and YY1 is independently placed in COVID-19 and separately in ovarian cancer by retrieved papers, and their target lists intersect on TP53/CDKN1A/MYC, so the module is nameable and partly evidenced — but no retrieved paper connects COVID-19 and ovarian cancer through this axis, so the cross-disease link is inference from two independently well-established roles, not a documented joint fact.
support: PMID 36180527 (TFDP1-linked complex mediates SARS-CoV-2 Nsp6 damage to cardiomyocytes); PMID 38614125 (ZNF146 drives ovarian cancer cell-cycle progression via TFDP1); PMID 34571838 (KAT5 depletion accompanies oxidative stress/senescence in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells); PMID 35392432 (KAT5 inhibition suppresses PD-L1 in ovarian cancer); PMID 40668819 (SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a interacts with YY1); PMID 41072350 (YY1/HIF1A drives ovarian cancer angiogenesis); PMID 40867514 (YY1 as a central node in ovarian cancer drug resistance); PMID 40890129 (YY1-induced USP43 suppresses ferroptosis in ovarian cancer); PMID 42134086 (YY1-linked lactylation drives bevacizumab resistance in ovarian cancer).
how_to_falsify: In SARS-CoV-2-infected epithelial/cardiac cells, ChIP for KAT5, TFDP1 and YY1 at the CDKN1A/TP53 loci and test whether their occupancy or the acetylation mark they deposit actually changes with infection; in parallel, knock down TFDP1 and YY1 in ovarian cancer lines with and without KAT5 inhibition and measure whether PD-L1, angiogenic output and proliferation drop synergistically (as expected for a shared node) versus independently. If viral infection does not measurably alter KAT5/TFDP1/YY1 occupancy at these shared targets, or if the ovarian-cancer phenotypes from perturbing each factor are additive/independent rather than converging on the same targets, the shared-checkpoint account is wrong.
caveats: Blood (COVID-19) versus ovary (ovarian cancer) is a systemic-versus-local tissue pairing, and the 64 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so apparent recurrence is not 64 independent replications. THRA and RARG had the highest or near-highest recurrence (32/64 and 28/64) and strong Open Targets association for both diseases, but THRA's retrieved literature was uniformly judged unrelated to either disease and RARG's only COVID-19 hit is a coincidental AML case report from the pandemic period, not a mechanistic link — both were left out of the programme rather than forced in. NR5A1, MXD1, SOX6, IRX5, ZNF256, AIRE and FOXP4 had ovarian-cancer or COVID-only support but did not fit a single coherent module with the others and were not used. The single-view exclusions (AKNA, GFI1, etc.) and tissue-generic exclusions (NFATC1, TWIST1, RUNX2, PRDM1, etc.) show that obvious immune- or hormone-tissue master regulators were already screened out before this account was built, so the module named here is not a default fallback.
